title: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — Section 10 (Power of Entry and Inspection)

content.overview: Section 10 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 confers power of entry and inspection for the purposes of the Act. Any person empowered by the Central Government may enter any place at reasonable times with necessary assistance for performing functions under the Act, examining equipment or industrial plant, conducting tests, and taking samples, subject to the statutory conditions. Occupiers and persons in charge must render assistance as required.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Is the officer empowered under s. 10? (2) Entry at reasonable time with assistance? (3) Purpose within the Act (examine, test, sample)? (4) Occupier cooperation?
content.study:
s. 10 is an enforcement-enabling power. Validity of inspection often turns on empowerment, purpose and manner.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Empowered person
sections.body: Any person empowered by the Central Government in this behalf may exercise entry and inspection powers.

sections.heading: Entry and purposes
sections.body: Enter any place at all reasonable times with necessary assistance to perform functions under the Act, including examining plant/equipment, conducting searches/tests and taking samples as the section provides.

sections.heading: Duty to assist
sections.body: Every person carrying on industry, operation or process or handling hazardous substances must render all assistance to the empowered person.

sections.heading: Link to sampling
sections.body: s. 11 deals specifically with power to take samples; s. 10 is the broader entry/inspection frame.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Prove empowerment, reasonable time, statutory purpose and any resistance or non-cooperation on the facts.

examples.title: Plant inspection
examples.body: An empowered officer enters a factory at a reasonable time to examine emission control equipment under s. 10 — occupier must assist.

hypotheticals.question: Can any police officer enter under s. 10 without Central empowerment?
hypotheticals.analysis: s. 10 requires a person empowered by the Central Government in this behalf; general police powers are not a substitute.

distinctions.title: s. 10 entry/inspection vs s. 11 samples
distinctions.left: Broad power of entry, examination and inspection.
distinctions.right: Specific power and procedure to take samples of air, water, soil or other substance.

misconceptions.trap: s. 10 allows entry at any hour without reasonableness.
misconceptions.correction: The section contemplates entry at all reasonable times with necessary assistance for Act purposes.
